correctness.rationale: Direct coordinate witnesses handle different supports; two opposite signs with a common first + sign handle equal supports over real AND complex scalars via \(|1+\lambda|^2+|1-\lambda|^2=2+2|\lambda|^2\). Projective representatives are distinct. The exact ratio \(2(n-k)/(k+1)\) identifies the maximizing layer. Binomial-mode Stirling expansion proves the coefficient and exponent analytically. The included verify.py recomputes all sampled layers from code in this same package, including 475172 pairwise exact real orthogonality checks. No finite computation is presented as proof of the all-dimensions theorem.

value.rationale: The dimension-dependence of maximum mutually Birkhoff–James orthogonal families is an explicit open quantitative theme in the 2021 primary paper. The earlier displayed full-support family grows at base 2, whereas a natural uniform-support union of signed projective cube faces grows at base 3 up to a sharp \(n^{-1/2}\) factor. The structural cross-support lemma establishes why the supports can be combined without losing pairwise orthogonality. This is a substantial exponential improvement in a standard invariant, not an isolated small-case computation, arbitrary unmotivated slice, or claim of exact graph maximum.
